## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D GTA5-style browser game from the empty static repo.
- Implement open-world top-down city, driving, shooting, wanted system, missions, HUD, audio, and mobile controls.

## Requirements
- User asked for “2D GTA5” as a build request.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly at completion.
- Must be complete and playable, not a prototype.
- Support Android/iOS responsive layouts and usable touch controls, per repo conventions.
- Static deployment must expose `index.html`.

## Decisions
- Built as pure HTML/CSS/JS with Canvas 2D and no external assets or build step.
- Created a Los Santos-inspired open world with procedural roads, buildings, beach, pier, parks, traffic, pedestrians, cops, vehicles, weapons, day/night cycle, and procedural audio.
- Implemented five-mission story chain: `FIRST GEAR`, `PIER PRESSURE`, `EVIDENCE RUN`, `BEACH CLEANUP`, `KING OF THE CITY`.
- Added localStorage save/continue, free roam ending, wanted stars, Pay ’n’ Spray, Ammu-Nation, safehouse heal/save, pickups, deaths/respawns, pause/end screens.
- Exposed `window.__ls` debug handle for automated playtesting.

## Work State

### Completed
- Created `index.html`, `style.css`, `game.js` (large monolithic module).
- Title screen, HUD, radar, mission UI, pause/fail/end overlays, touch controls all implemented.
- World generation and rendering, vehicles/traffic, pedestrians, cops, bullets, particles, decals, explosions, day/night lighting.
- All five missions implemented and verified end-to-end via Playwright with no page errors.
- Mission 1 completion, save, next-mission marker, SMG unlock, armor reward, final ending flow verified.
- Driving fixed: desktop throttle/steering previously always read empty touch state; now uses `isTouch` branch.
- Mission target vehicle cleanup fixed so player no longer remains inside an invisible removed car.
- Shooting verified: civilian killed, wanted level rose to 1, ammo decremented.
- Mobile layout verified at `390x844` with touch UI visible and no errors.
- Static server running on `http://localhost:3000` via tmux session `lsgame`.
- Browser Playwright installed and working.

### Active
- Polishing title screen and mobile/gameplay visuals.
- Reviewing remaining issues:
  - Wanted stars appeared possibly stale after `clearWanted()` in a test screenshot; verify computed classes/state.
  - Mission banner says generic “MISSION” kicker even for “MISSION PASSED” / “MISSION FAILED”.
  - Stale delayed “NEXT JOB” toast can fire after the next mission starts.
  - Title background is quite dark/repetitive; consider title-only brightness or better cinematic camera.
  - Player sprite is small; consider subtle glow/outline for visibility.
  - Add favicon to stop `favicon.ico` 404 console noise.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Fix minor UI/state issues: stale wanted stars, mission banner kicker, delayed next-job toast cancellation, favicon.
2. Improve title background and player visibility if time permits.
3. Re-test mobile title/game screenshots and desktop gameplay after changes.
4. Verify death/respawn, pause menu, continue/save, cops/explosions, and ending screen with Playwright.
5. Commit changes and briefly note assumptions in final response.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: all game logic, world, entities, missions, rendering, input, UI.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: DOM structure for canvas, HUD, title/pause/fail/end screens, touch controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css`: full responsive visual design and touch-control layout.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: generated verification screenshots including `title2.png`, `start2.png`, `drive.png`, `mission1.png`, `end.png`, `shoot.png`, `mobile_title.png`, `mobile_game.png`.

## Important Context
- Server command: `PORT=3000 node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs"` in tmux session `lsgame`.
- Playwright custom test scripts live in `/tmp/opencode/`: `shot.mjs`, `test_drive.mjs`, `test_mission.mjs`, `test_allmissions.mjs`, `test_shoot.mjs`, `test_mobile.mjs`, `title_shots.mjs`.
- Playwright module import path used: `/home/runner/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/node_modules/playwright/index.mjs`.
- Screenshot CLI `--filename` often times out; use custom Playwright script with `timeout: 60000`.
- `window.__ls` exposes `state`, `player`, `vehicles`, `people`, `camera`, `world`, `keys`, `audio`, `startMission`, `completeMission`, `failMission`, `clearWanted`, `respawnPlayer`, `getMissionMarker`, `getInteraction`, `districtAt`, `teleport`, `giveMoney`, `setHeat`.
- Current code passes `node --check game.js`.
- No commit has been made yet; working tree changes are uncommitted.
- Test output confirmed mission progression: money after missions 1–4 = `$10,550`; after mission 5 = `$25,550`; `smgUnlocked=true`; free roam true.
- Mission banner duration currently 3.2s and can obscure center-screen action.
- Title logo appears pink due heavy shadow/stroke styling, but is intentional-looking.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.
